Ademetionine produced a good or excellent clinical response in patients with hepatic steatosis.7 In a study8 of patients with alcoholic liver cirrhosis, treated with ademetionine for 2 years, there was a trend towards reduced overall mortality or need for liver transplantation, but only in patients with less severe hepatic dysfunction. However, a systematic review9 of 9 randomised placebo-controlled studies, which included the latter study could not find evidence to support or refute the claim that ademetionine has a beneficial effect in patients with alcoholic liver diseases, and larger high quality randomised placebo-controlled studies are needed. 1.
